10. The Section on Intermediate Duration of Karma (15r8–15v11) [1.
The Procedure for Taking the Vows, etc.]
Having prostrated with my whole being to the Vajrācārya, the great guru, I shall explain the ritual manual for the mandala in accordance with the *Śrī-guhyasamāja*. 1.1.

[1.2 Preliminary Service] One who knows the procedure for the preliminary service, who has received instruction from the guru, who is skillful, who has recited the vidyā, who is free from signs [of attachment], and who has performed protection on all sides; || 1.2 ||
For the sake of his disciples and for the accumulation of merit, he was earnestly requested by his disciples to perform the rite of ritual expansion and the act of drawing the mandala. (1.3)
One should first perform that which has been taught, the supreme method of the Vajrācārya;
for seven or eight days, one should prescribe a diet of the three white foods.
Rice, milk, and ghee— these three constitute the common meal;
one should eat ghee and curd for as long as a full day and night on the first lunar day (pratipad).
This procedure should be performed by the wise who are intent upon merit;
for them, there is no doubt that they will obtain the food of the nectar of Dharma. 1.6.
Furthermore, O Mother, why is this so?
Because the Vajrācārya who possesses great wealth is the one in whose presence the maṇḍala should be drawn.
One should draw [the maṇḍala] there, having likewise generated the thought of awakening (bodhicitta) that follows the three times. || 1.7 ||
Having placed faith in the Three Jewels, being free from doubt and compassionate by nature, [one should undertake the vows]. [1.4 Undertaking the Vows] [1.4.1 The Three Vows]
And on the eighth and fourteenth [lunar days], this is to be accomplished by those living as householders.
Now, I shall explain in due order, according to what is appropriate and fitting, the supreme ritual procedure for renunciants who are knowledgeable in the rules on the full moon day.
Being devoted to the thought of awakening, one should not be intent on longing for other deities; for one should have faith in the Three Jewels and be inclined and directed toward them. 1.10
One who possesses faith should avoid taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, falsehood, and intoxicants;
and regarding food, [one should avoid] taking what is not given... falsehood?
Having established himself in the yoga of the house, he should accomplish the threefold concentration.
Furthermore, having fully undertaken the threefold restraint, the renunciant should practice;
moreover, the three concentrations are established elsewhere through resolute conviction. (1.12)
[1.4.2 Vajrasaṃvara] Since it has been taught in other tantras, we have merely spoken of the three vows here; now the Vajrasaṃvara is being explained. || 1.13 ||

[The Fourfold Prostration] Oṃ, I offer myself for the service and worship of all Tathāgatas; O Vajrasattva of all Tathāgatas, empower me! Oṃ, I offer myself for the empowerment of all Tathāgatas; O Vajraratna of all Tathāgatas, confer the empowerment upon me!
Oṃ, I offer myself to the ongoing worship of all Tathāgatas; O Vajradharma of all Tathāgatas, set me in motion!
Oṃ, I offer myself for the ritual activity of worship of all Tathāgatas; O Vajrakarma of all Tathāgatas, act upon me!
Then, having formed the vajrāñjali mudrā, the wise one should bow with his head;
he should offer his hands joined in añjali, filled with flowers, to the Jinas.
Having likewise placed it upon his heart, the wise man should bow it toward his forehead;
having brought it down from the forehead, he should touch his head with it and then prostrate with words.
[The Arising of the Bodhicitta] Immediately after the prostration: May the eternal Akṣobhya, Ratnāgrya, Lokeśa, and Amoghasiddhi attend to me!
The Tathāgatas, goddesses, and Bodhisattvas— the sons of the Victors— residing in the infinite and boundless world-systems of the ten directions.
I, named so-and-so,
from this moment until reaching the seat of enlightenment.
I generate the supreme, unsurpassed mind of awakening, just as the Protectors of the three times have made their resolve for perfect enlightenment. 1.16
I firmly undertake the threefold training in ethical discipline: the morality of gathering virtuous qualities and the morality of acting for the welfare of sentient beings. 1.17

[The Buddha Family]: One should take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha—the supreme, unsurpassed Three Jewels—for the sake of acting for the benefit of sentient beings. (Note: *sattvārthaṃ kriyāśīlam* is attested in the manuscript; moreover, the reading without *ca* is also supported by reliable sources!)
From this day forward, I shall maintain the vow born of the secret yoga.
I accept the vajra, the bell, and the mudrā according to reality;
and I shall accept the master in the sublime assembly of the Great Vajra Family.
I shall bestow the fourfold gift six times every day, within the yoga of the Great Jewel Family, at the delightful occasion. 1.20
I accept the true Dharma— outer, secret, and belonging to the three vehicles— within the pure Great Lotus Family, which gives rise to great awakening. 1.21
I truly accept the vow associated with all [the families],
in accordance with my capacity for the rites of worship within the great accumulation of the Karma family. (1.22)
Having generated the supreme, unsurpassed mind of awakening,
he has undertaken the complete vow for the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings. (1.23)
I shall cause those who have not crossed over to cross; I shall liberate those who are not liberated;
I shall give rest to those who are weary, and I shall establish all beings in final nirvana.
[1.5 Closing Verse] By this,
the Guru, together with his assembly of disciples, shall become free from transgressions.
One should break through calamities even with very slight obstacles.
[26] This is the procedure for undertaking the vows and so forth.
